speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, I wish I could report that the problem has been solved, that, actually, nothing needs to be done.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As the Senior Minister of State Sim Ann said recently, “Across many communities... our sense is that residential smoking has risen”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Since our Motion, many Singaporeans have spoken up.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On social media, in news media and in private messages, they report feeling tortured and trapped by their neighbours’ second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will share the stories of these Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will also share that a law already exists that makes smoking near windows and at balconies illegal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I will emphasise the power of deterrence, not just enforcement of this current law against smoking near windows and at balconies, but deterrence, a power that we have not sufficiently drawn on.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, let me provide a reminder to this House on how deadly second-hand smoke is.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Deaths from motor accidents, the coronavirus and workplace injuries are all serious and all need our attention.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, I have regularly spoken up on these very issues in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My point is that second-hand smoke needs our urgent attention, too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Unlike these other causes of death, there is no preventive measure you can take against second-hand smoke at home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: You can install an air purifier but, as MOH has said, it does not work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: You can shut your windows but, as many residents know, it does not work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: You can talk to your neighbours but, again, as many residents know, more often than not, it does not work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One resident, Kim, shared with me about how she begged her neighbour, with her baby in her arms, about how his second-hand smoke was affecting her child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: You can move house like another resident, Jennifer, did.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She has moved house three times in the past six years and has been unlucky enough to suffer from her neighbours’ second-hand smoke every time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She recently wrote to me at 1.30 am, saying, “Our neighbour is smoking and we are unable to sleep.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are literally dying in our sleep every day”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And honestly, how many people can afford to move house repeatedly to avoid the dangers of second-hand smoke?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Condominium residents do not have it any better.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MCSTs have no power to fine their residents, regardless of their bylaws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A condominium resident, NC, spoke to her neighbour, who smokes throughout the day at her balcony and was told that what she was doing was legal despite the condominium bylaw prohibiting smoking at the balcony.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: NC is worried about the health of her two young children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, let us focus on how this affects our children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We all become sick from second-hand smoke, but the worst is saved for our children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Parents write letters to me and they describe their lived experiences in these exact words.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Their letters sometimes read like horror stories; they know something is killing their children, but they are helpless to do anything about it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Take Ying Ying, a young mother with one child and another on the way.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Her neighbour’s smoking has plagued her family for four years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It caused her firstborn to suffer from bronchitis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She is now terrified that her next child will suffer the same.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To quote her, “Every time we want to open the windows for fresh air, we hesitate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because we never know how much shorter our breath will become”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: His elder son is taking PSLE this year and studies at home while inhaling his neighbour’s second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: His younger son has been coughing and sick as a result of the second-hand smoke. “It does not make sense to suffer like that,” Peter says.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Kelvin shared with me about how he has a family member who has cancer and they are worried that the constant exposure to second-hand smoke will be bad for her already failing health.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As he puts it, “We are losing our freedom for fresh air”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have always taken pride in being a safe nation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But for many, home is no longer a safe place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is the place where their neighbours cause them to suffer asthma attacks, bronchitis, breathlessness, respiratory infections and they cannot do anything about it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Health Promotion Board states, “You wouldn't put your child in danger by letting him play with fire.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, why risk your child’s heath by exposing him or her to second-hand smoke?” I am sure many parents agree with that.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, like me, they choose not to smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But they have no choice when it comes to someone else’s second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Here, we should remember that one of the most powerful forces in Singapore is deterrence.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, it is fair to say that deterrence is at the cornerstone of our law and order.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It explains why we have such low crime rates.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we know that deterrence does not happen out of thin air.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a three-tier approach and you need to build it, starting from the bottom.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At the first tier, you must make clear that the bad behaviour is illegal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To be clear, the Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) for Sustainability and the Environment is not calling for smoking at home to be illegal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We know that it will be almost impossible to enforce a ban on smoking at home and there will be no deterrent effect of such a law as people will not be able to see people smoking inside their homes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even without doing anything else, it would already reduce the problem of second-hand smoke in homes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure Senior Minister of State Amy Khor would agree with me that Singapore is, generally, a nation of law abiders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would also help neighbours mediate, as offenders can no longer say that their behaviour is perfectly legal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would help give more bite to NEA officers who already give advisories to those smoking near windows and at balconies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Their words would have more impact if backed by the law.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 43 can already be used to stop smoking near windows and at balconies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this unprecedented period of home-based learning and work from home, this needs be done urgently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our authorities have historically been very good at this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have all seen signs by the Police warning against scams, thefts and molestation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, we can make it clear that smoking near windows and at balconies is illegal under current laws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We can then leverage the new LCD screens at HDB lobbies to start an awareness campaign.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These screens are near to where offences happen and are most likely to have a significant impact.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singaporeans respond when they know something is illegal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is the point Senior Minister of State Amy Khor took issue with when we raised our Motion last year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To quote her: “Cameras must capture the smokers smoking or holding a lighted cigarette as evidence for enforcement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, a smoker can easily hide behind a pillar, frosted glass, windows or curtains to avoid detection by the cameras.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Overall, this may entail deployment of significant resources without achieving effective outcomes." Let me first clarify that a smoker is unlikely to hide behind pillars, windows or curtains to smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a former smoker, I can tell you that smokers smoke at open windows and balconies precisely to get the smoke out of their homes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would defeat the purpose to hide behind some cover.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If they do hide, like how Senior Minister of State Amy Khor describes, then it would be a good thing, not a bad thing, because it would help contain most of the smoke within their homes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor's concern is also about the cost and effectiveness of camera surveillance, but camera surveillance is just one of the many options.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I cannot imagine a person continuing to smoke at their windows, committing an offence right in front of their neighbours in the nearby block.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure some neighbours will take photos of this and report the smoker or put it on social media.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Deterrence, again, will kick in, before the need for enforcement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For a small number of cases where smokers continue to smoke at windows and balconies, then enforcement kicks in.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We start with advisories and then nuisance orders under the Environmental Public Health Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I have mentioned earlier, NEA officers already issue advisories today.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But they are not backed by the threat of harsher penalties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There will be cases where the culprit repeats the offences despite the advisories or nuisance orders and stronger enforcement is needed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To collect further evidence, we can first draw on evidence from complainants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Complainants are often very capable of collecting evidence on their own.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, we already ask residents to provide evidence of their neighbours smoking, such as photos or videos, when they bring a case to the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It already does this for high-rise littering and bird feeders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Both of these problems kill far less people than second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are not asking for surveillance cameras to be placed everywhere, throughout Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These cameras are used by the authorities today to catch high-rise litterbugs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But they will actually work just as effectively for catching those smoking at windows and balconies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These photos show how these cameras can already capture someone smoking at their windows without invading the privacy of the smokers and their neighbours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will share these photos on my social media pages so everyone can see for themselves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The good news also is that NEA has improved technology.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This has helped to reduce the need for enforcement officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But in the case of smoking near windows or at balconies, the chances of a successful enforcement are much higher as compared to high-rise littering.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If we can catch someone throwing litter from their window in a fleeting moment, action that takes a couple of seconds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Then surely, we can catch someone smoking at the window for a few minutes at a time repeatedly throughout the day.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The chances of catching someone smoking at the window are also infinitely higher than the odds of catching someone right inside their own homes naked.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the Police are able to enforce the law against being naked at home, then surely NEA can enforce the current law against smoking at windows and balconies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is no law where we enforce 100% of the time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We obviously do not have speeding cameras on every single road.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the same way, we would not need to install surveillance cameras at every housing estate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Instead, what we need to do is enforce some cases and then publicise them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will make clear that the authorities can and will take action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is what we already do with so many public health hazards where universal enforcement is not possible: racing on roads, cycling on highways, PMDs on pavements, being naked in your own home, feeding of birds and so on.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We clean up a few bad eggs, we announce it to all Singaporeans and we make a point.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this COVID-19 pandemic, we have tried so hard to keep people safe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Deterrence is a power we have not used enough.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Everyone is well aware of the harmful effects of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It has also been found that exposure to second-hand smoke during pregnancy increases the risk of stillbirth, congenital malformations and respiratory illnesses.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: With such comprehensive findings, it is evident that second-hand smoke has the same adverse toxic chemicals that smokers inhale.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: There is no safe degree of exposure for passive smoke.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Unfortunately, I happen to be a passive smoker.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I am residing above a neighbour who smokes by his window numerous times a day.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: A window is meant for natural air ventilation and definitely not for cigarette smoke to be emitted into our homes.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Hence, whenever my neighbour below smokes, I will have to keep my window closed.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: On the other hand, I have a considerate neighbour who would take his smoke breaks near the car park a few times a day.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The neighbour does this because he does not wish to expose his young son and his wife to his second-hand smoke.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Over the past year, many of my Sembawang West residents have sent me troubling emails about them being exposed to second-hand smoke emitted by their neighbours.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Given the rising number of people having to work from home as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, this will be a concern that we will have to address.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I am certain that there are numerous similar complaints that my fellow Members of Parliament in this House have had to deal with.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Most of the time attending to such complaints do not end well and would usually be compromising the much-needed harmonious environment amongst neighbours.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: There is absolutely nothing anyone can do to help the innocent victims of second-hand smokers.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: While we can understand that it is not possible for a smoker to be able to quit smoking easily, it is important for smokers to understand that they need to be considerate and behave like my other neighbour who walks to a smoking or an open area to smoke.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It is not fair to expose non-smokers to the dangerous toxic chemicals caused by cigarette smoke – period.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Smokers must always remind themselves to smoke only at allocated spots.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Under the Smoking Act, there is a list of places where smoking is allowed; some of these locations include open spaces in residential estates and town centres, surface car parks, top deck of multistorey car parks and uncovered walkways.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Unfortunately, it is often seen that most smokers light up wherever convenient for them.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Similarly, I would also like to clarify section 43 of the Environment Public Health Act.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The intent of this Act is to protect residents from any fumes, vapours, example, in any premises which are dangerous to health.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Then, should second-hand smoke from cigarettes not be included in this category?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Separately, we should continue to have targets to bring down the number of smokers over the next five to 10 years.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Our National Tobacco Control Programme introduced in 1986 had a long-term strategy to make Singapore a “nation of non-smokers”.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In 2018 we had announced a target to bring the smoking rate down to below 10% by 2020.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Personally, I believe that many smokers do wish to stop smoking but being addicted to the habit, it is often easier said than done.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It would be good if we could introduce more aggressive campaigns to help those who sincerely wish to stop smoking and also to introduce a convincing message on the dangers of smoking to our children at an early age.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Singapore must continue to inch steadily towards achieving a “nation of non-smokers”.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The home is now an office for most working Singaporeans and with that growing trend, we must consider the circumstances that non-smoking Singaporeans are in.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Their home now substitutes an office which is often located in a commercial district.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Offices in all commercial districts do not allow smoking.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: If you wish to smoke while working in a commercial office, you will have to go downstairs to an allocated area to smoke.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We are simply requesting for some consideration for smokers not to smoke at their windows or balconies.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: There is no doubt that second-hand smoke threatens public health and social harmony.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In residential areas, this includes common corridors and stairwells of apartment blocks, right up to the doorstep.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are now looking into extending the smoking prohibition to even more places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Poh Li San have asked my Ministry to prohibit smoking at windows and balconies to minimise second-hand smoke drift.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We appreciate their intent but as previously explained during a Motion on the same issue in October last year, enforcement is not simple.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, let me clarify the intent of sections 43, 44 and 45 in Part V of the Environmental Public Health Act or EPHA, which are on the abatement of public nuisances through the use of Nuisance Orders and explain why they cannot be used to prohibit smoking at windows and balconies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This part of the EPHA was enacted in the context of 1960s Singapore to provide for quick mitigative action to arrest public nuisances from specific industrial activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It is not the purpose of the EPHA to deal with smoking prohibition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is why the Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act was enacted in 1970.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Part V of the EPHA addresses public nuisances that affect the public at large and not private nuisances which interfere with another person’s use or enjoyment of his property, which is the situation with smoking in homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To achieve deterrence, not only do we need the appropriate law, we also need effective enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Unfortunately, NEA’s assessment is that this is not achievable with current enforcement modalities and technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: If we were to prohibit smoking at windows and balconies, we can be sure that there will be smokers who will find ways to avoid getting caught.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They could smoke in balcony corners, or in toilets with windows or ventilation fans, which some already do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Smoke will inevitably seep out and can still travel to neighbouring units.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We cannot prosecute people based solely on complaints of smell or smoke wafting from neighbouring units.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have to catch the offender in the act of smoking at the balcony or window, or have witnesses come forward to testify that they witnessed the act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Yet complainants are often unable to accurately identify the source of the smell or smoke.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Each case will require extensive manpower and resources to investigate, with no guarantee of successful enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Furthermore, to undertake investigation, we will need to accept significant social trade-offs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As noted, smokers who want to evade enforcement are unlikely to stand in full view at the balcony or window.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To clearly capture a person in the act of smoking at windows and balconies, cameras would have to be of a sufficient resolution and trained directly into units.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Their field of view would also cover neighbouring units and potentially include innocent neighbours engaged in other activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These are just some of the many challenges faced in catching the culprit, given current technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Residents could become even more frustrated, as there is a law but with great enforcement difficulties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even for high-rise littering, where there has been a significant number of successful enforcements, many still express frustration that offenders have not been caught, an issue that has also been discussed in this House.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As people spend more time at home nowadays, NEA has stepped up its enforcement efforts in HDB estates to address the issue of second-hand smoke in homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While this would be of little comfort to our Members Mr Louis Ng and Ms Poh Li San, Singapore is not alone in grappling with this intractable issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Other jurisdictions have attempted regulation and when doing so, they have done so on a very selective basis, and more importantly, they have not experienced clear success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Non-compliance could result in the termination of the tenant's lease, a huge consequence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The situation improved in the first month but, within a year, the situation had reverted to what it had been previously, as smokers resumed smoking at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While the consequences were real and serious, the chances of being caught were not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We also need to recognise that there are wide-ranging views on this issue, which touches fundamentally on an individual's right in his own home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Prohibiting smoking in homes, even if just at windows and balconies, is controversial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Homes are private spaces and it can be viewed as intrusive for governments to regulate what people can and cannot do there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The legislation did not garner enough votes and was not enacted as some tenants contended that the ban would infringe on their personal rights inside their homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For Singapore, we must address this potentially divisive issue in a way which strengthens rather than hinders our efforts to cultivate a gracious and cohesive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, residents are coming together to discuss ground-up solutions to address neighbourly issues, including second-hand smoke in homes under the Municipal Services Office or MSO's "Love Our 'Hood" initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also keep a lookout for innovations and technological solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will monitor the outcome of this latest pilot study on the effectiveness of DSPs to reduce smoking in homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Technological solutions that remove second-hand smoke at source or prevent its drift could bring reprieve to affected residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We hope to see promising submissions from enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The pandemic has been a difficult time for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For many, this has led to heightened tensions and fewer interactions among neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Where there are problems of second-hand smoke from homes, I encourage neighbours to communicate with one another as a first step towards resolving the matter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My Ministry has worked with various agencies to enhance joint advisories issued to smokers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My Ministry is also part of a workgroup that is reviewing the Community Dispute Management Framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are proposing enhancements to increase the effectiveness of the community mediation process and the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The workgroup will share updates in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I want to assure Members that we are committed to tackling second-hand smoke from homes and are monitoring global best practices and developments in technology and legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We stay open to innovative and practicable solutions and will continue to draw on the ideas and efforts of all stakeholders to address this issue for a more gracious and cohesive society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The whole Adjournment Motion is about using deterrence, not enforcement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am just wondering whether MSE feels that if there is a law, whether there will be a deterrent effect and whether there is going to be a need where 100% of Singaporeans do not comply with the law?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I cannot imagine that to be the case and I wonder whether Senior Minister of State Amy Khor can share her views on that.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, for deterrence to be effective – obviously, when you have a legislation, it is for deterrence.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The time allowed for the proceedings has expired.
